content.user_title: Design Mobile Games for Touch and Stores
content.value_statement: Mobile games often fail when desktop design assumptions are reused on phones. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code plan touch controls, performance, battery use, store needs, and monetization.
actual_capabilities: Summarizes mobile platform constraints such as touch input, battery, thermal limits, screen size, and interruptions.
Provides touch input guidance, including large targets, feedback, gesture support, and reduced precision demands.
Outlines performance targets for thermal management, battery savings, frame rate limits, and paused states.
Lists basic App Store and Google Play considerations, including privacy labels, screenshots, API targets, and bundles.
Compares monetization models for premium games, in-app purchases, ads, and subscriptions.
Identifies mobile game anti-patterns such as desktop controls, forced orientation, and always-on networking.
limitations: It provides design principles, not a complete mobile game implementation.
It does not include engine-specific code for Unity, Godot, Unreal, iOS, or Android.
Store requirements can change, so current App Store and Google Play policies still need verification.
It cannot measure real device performance without profiling data from target hardware.

use_cases.title: Plan a Touch-First Prototype
use_cases.description: Convert a desktop game idea into mobile controls with larger targets, gestures, and reduced precision demands.

use_cases.title: Review Mobile Readiness
use_cases.description: Check an existing game concept for battery, thermal, orientation, interruption, and network risks before development.

use_cases.title: Prepare Store Launch Notes
use_cases.description: Create a checklist for screenshots, privacy labels, account deletion, API targets, bundles, and monetization choices.

prompt_templates.title: Review My Mobile Game Idea
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this mobile game idea for touch input, screen size, battery use, interruptions, and store readiness: [describe the game].

prompt_templates.title: Convert Desktop Controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert these desktop controls into a touch-first mobile control scheme. Include target sizes, gestures, feedback, and ways to avoid precise timing: [controls].

prompt_templates.title: Create a Performance Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a mobile performance plan for this game. Cover frame rate, thermal triggers, paused states, network use, and battery-saving tradeoffs: [game details].

prompt_templates.title: Audit Launch Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this mobile game launch plan for App Store, Google Play, monetization, privacy, screenshots, orientation, and anti-pattern risks: [launch plan].

output_examples.input: A rhythm platformer designed for keyboard controls.
output: Reduce strict timing windows for mobile play.
Use large jump and slide zones with immediate visual feedback.
Add a 30 FPS mode and pause effects when the device gets hot.

output_examples.input: A casual puzzle game preparing for iOS and Android release.
output: Prepare privacy labels and screenshots for all required device sizes.
Confirm account deletion support if accounts are created.
Use app bundles for Google Play and check the target API requirement.

output_examples.input: A free multiplayer game with ads and progression purchases.
output: Review whether ads fit the expected session length.
Cache noncritical data and avoid always-on network use.
Monitor thermal behavior during long multiplayer sessions.

best_practices: Design controls around fingers, screen occlusion, and large hit areas from the first prototype.
Set clear thermal and battery targets before adding visual effects or network features.
Review store requirements and monetization choices before final production.
anti_patterns: Copying desktop controls directly onto a phone screen.
Ignoring battery drain, thermal throttling, and paused states.
Treating App Store and Google Play requirements as final-week release tasks.

faq.question: Does this skill generate game code?
faq.answer: It focuses on design and planning guidance. It can help structure tasks before implementation.

faq.question: Can it help with Unity or Godot projects?
faq.answer: Yes, it can review mobile design choices for those projects, but it does not provide engine-specific APIs.

faq.question: Does it cover App Store and Google Play launch needs?
faq.answer: It covers common launch considerations. You should still verify current platform policies before release.

faq.question: Can it improve battery and thermal performance?
faq.answer: It suggests planning strategies such as frame limits, sleeping while paused, and reducing effects when devices get hot.

faq.question: Is this useful for non-game mobile apps?
faq.answer: Some touch and battery principles may apply, but the skill is written for mobile game development.

faq.question: Does it choose a monetization model?
faq.answer: It compares common models and helps identify fit. Final pricing and business decisions remain with the team.
